tool.name: HyphAeon-Disease
tool.description: Disease variant effect prediction and pathogenicity scoring
tool.command: @SYMLINK_FILES_NO_TREE@ #if $mutations_source.source_type == "file" and $mutations_source.mutations_file: ln -s '$mutations_source.mutations_file' mutations_input.csv && #end if hyphaeon disease -a input.$input_file.extension @MODEL_SOURCE@ -m #if $mutations_source.source_type == "file": mutations_input.csv #else '$mutations_source.mutations_text' #end if #if $canonical_seq: --canonical-seq '$canonical_seq' #end if #if $human_taxon: --human-taxon '$human_taxon' #end if @OUTPUTS@

param.name: source_type
param.label: Mutation input method
param.help: Provide mutations as inline text or upload a CSV/Parquet file

param.name: mutations_text
param.label: Mutations
param.help: Comma-separated list of mutations in standard notation (e.g. 'R175H,G245S,R248Q')

param.name: mutations_file
param.label: Mutations file
param.help: CSV, TSV, or Parquet file containing mutation identifiers (e.g. 'R175H,G245S' or one per row)

param.name: canonical_seq
param.label: Canonical reference sequence (optional)
param.help: Canonical human reference sequence (FASTA file or raw amino acid string). Used for coordinate mapping between canonical positions and MSA columns.

param.name: human_taxon
param.label: Human taxon name (optional)
param.help: Name of the human reference taxon in the alignment (auto-detected if omitted). Use this when the alignment header does not contain obvious human identifiers.

tool.help:
HyphAeon Disease: Clinical Variant Effect Prediction & Pathogenicity Scoring ===============================================================================
**What question does this method answer?**
For a set of clinical variants (e.g., cancer-associated mutations in TP53), which are likely pathogenic versus benign? How does each mutation disrupt the deep evolutionary constraints learned by the model?
**How it works**
HyphAeon uses its phylogenetic foundation model to score the pathogenicity of amino acid substitutions. Given a codon alignment containing a human reference sequence and a list of mutations (e.g., R175H), the tool:
1. Maps canonical protein coordinates to MSA columns using dynamic programming alignment against the human reference sequence in the alignment. 2. For each mutation, substitutes the wild-type codon with the mutant amino acid and measures the change in the model's selection signal (ΔLRT). 3. Converts the perturbation score to a pathogenicity probability and classification (pathogenic / likely pathogenic / benign / likely benign).
**Inputs**
- An in-frame codon alignment (FASTA or NEXUS) containing a human reference sequence - A list of mutations (inline text or CSV/Parquet file) in standard notation (e.g., R175H, G245S) - Optional canonical reference sequence for coordinate mapping - Optional explicit human taxon name (auto-detected if omitted)
**Outputs**
- **JSON**: full per-mutation results including canonical position, MSA column, mapping status, pathogenicity score, and prediction class - **CSV**: tabular per-mutation summary suitable for clinical reporting
